title: Soda ash (Solvay ammonia soda process)
route: Limestone is burnt with coke in shaft kilns; brine is ammoniated and carbonated with the kiln gas so sodium bicarbonate crystallises. The bicarbonate is filtered and calcined with steam to light soda ash, and the mother liquor is limed and steam stripped to recover the ammonia, leaving calcium chloride liquor as the effluent.
summary: 1,000 t/d light soda ash from 1.51 t salt and 1.16 t limestone per tonne, with 3.1 t of steam per tonne.

reactions.eq: NaCl + NH3 + CO2 + H2O -> NaHCO3 + NH4Cl

conditions: 950 to 1,100 C, kiln gas 41% CO2, burnt lime 77% CaO
Live 3.5 bar steam, bottoms about 115 C

greener.title: Natural trona soda ash, or capture the kiln CO2
greener.text: Soda ash refined from natural trona (as in Wyoming) avoids the lime kiln, the ammonia loop and the calcium chloride effluent and uses less energy. In a Solvay plant, venting less kiln gas, recovering distiller heat and selling the calcium chloride cut the footprint.

assumptions: Salt utilisation 73% in the carbonation towers (Hou: 'can average only 73 per cent'). Unreacted salt leaves with the distiller waste; no other salt losses are modelled.
Limestone 90% CaCO3 (BREF: 85 to 95%), rest lumped as silica; 95% of the CaCO3 burnt. Lime fed 5% over the fixed ammonia.

Coke is pure carbon burnt completely with just enough air; its rate is set so the kiln gas holds 41% CO2 (Hou). Real kilns make some CO (BREF: 4 to 20 kg/t). Kiln gas not needed in the towers is vented.
The ammonia loop carries the stoichiometric fixed ammonia plus 150 kg/t free ammonia and 273 kg/t dissolved CO2 (Hou). Losses are 0.3% of the loop, half to air and half to the distiller waste.

Distiller steam follows Hou's heat balance: heating the liquor from 45 C and milk of lime from 55 C to 115 C, decomposing ammonium bicarbonate, desorbing NH3 and CO2, plus 10% radiation. Milk of lime at 250 g CaO/L, sp. gr. 1.21 (Hou).
Calciner uses 40 bar steam to supply the reaction heat, evaporate 15% cake moisture and heat solids and gas to 180 C, plus 10% losses. Light soda ash only; no densification.
Brine purification chemicals, filter wash water, the brine washers and vacuum pumps are not modelled. Distiller waste density taken as 1.1 kg/L.

Equipment counts follow Hou's unit capacities (carbonation towers 110 t/d, filters 175 t/d, rotary calciners by shell area), so capex is conservative for a modern plant. Shaft kilns costed on the fired heater curve as a proxy, one kiln per 400 t/d of lime.
